record.original_question: Suppose that the polynomial equation F (w0 , w1 , ......, wn ) = 1 defines a smooth affine algebraic hypersurface (these are always parallellizable (Murthy, Swan, n=2; Suslin for general n). Can they be holomorphically immersed in C^n ?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $F\in\mathbb{C}[w_0,w_1,\dots,w_n]$ be a polynomial such that the affine algebraic hypersurface $X=\{(w_0,\dots,w_n)\in\mathbb{C}^{n+1}:F(w_0,\dots,w_n)=1\}$ is smooth. Such a hypersurface is known to be parallelizable, i.e., its holomorphic tangent bundle is trivial (by results of Murthy–Swan for $n=2$ and Suslin for general $n$). Determine whether every such smooth affine hypersurface $X$ admits a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}^n$ (where $n=\dim_{\mathbb{C}} X$); that is, whether there exists a holomorphic map $f:X\to\mathbb{C}^n$ whose differential $df_p:T_pX\to T_{f(p)}\mathbb{C}^n$ is injective at every point $p\in X$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not locate a definitive resolution of this question (whether every smooth affine algebraic hypersurface $F=1$ in $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ admits a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}^n$). Related general results on immersions and embeddings of Stein manifolds into Euclidean spaces exist (Eliashberg–Gromov, Forstnerič, Schürmann), but no source consulted asserts a complete answer to this specific minimal-target immersion problem for affine hypersurfaces.

status_evidence.title: Embeddings of Stein Manifolds of Dimension n into the affine space
status_evidence.snippet: There exist proper holomorphic embeddings of Stein manifolds of dimension n into C^q for the minimal integer q > (3n+1)/2.
status_evidence.claim: General results on Stein embeddings/immersions into affine space exist but address dimension thresholds above n; they do not settle the specific minimal case of n-dimensional affine hypersurfaces immersing into C^n.

status_evidence.title: Challenging problems on affine n-space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on affine spaces including parallelizability of hypersurfaces F=1.
status_evidence.claim: Parallelizability of smooth affine hypersurfaces F=1 in C^{n+1} is known (Murthy–Swan, Suslin), but the holomorphic immersion question into C^n is recorded as an open problem.
